title: Heard It
Twice

post.title: Why You Believe Things You've Heard Twice #shorts
post.description: Which 'fact' fooled you? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who still quotes the goldfish one. Theo has heard it a hundred times: goldfish forget everything in three seconds. (They don't: goldfish can remember things for months.) In 'Frequency and the Conference of Referential Validity' (Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior, 1977), Lynn Hasher, David Goldstein and Thomas Toppino showed people plausible trivia statements, some true and some false, in sessions two weeks apart. Statements they had seen before were rated as more likely to be true, whether they were true or not. Later work by Lisa Fazio and colleagues ('Knowledge Does Not Protect Against Illusory Truth', 2015) found repetition boosted belief even in statements that contradicted what people already knew. It's called the illusory truth effect: familiar feels easy, and easy feels true. #psychology #shorts #illusorytruth #misinformation #overthinking
